papers.title: From RNA design to delivery: Computational strategies for functional RNA therapeutics.
papers.abstract: RNA therapeutics provide a revolutionary means of treating a variety of diseases by precisely regulating gene expression and protein synthesis, with great medical significance. However, there are three key challenges to its clinical application: the inherent instability of RNA, the need for controlled regulation of RNA function, and the lack of an efficient delivery system. Computational strategies provide complementary tools for analyzing and optimizing RNA sequence, structure, function, and delivery, accelerating the rational design of RNAs and the optimization of delivery systems. This revi
papers.summary: This review surveys computational strategies that support the design, optimization, and delivery of RNA therapeutics, addressing RNA instability, the need for controlled functional regulation, and inefficient delivery systems. It highlights how in silico methods can accelerate rational RNA design and delivery vehicle optimization for clinical translation.

papers.title: Green synthesis of pyridine-benzofuran hybrids with anti-inflammatory activity alongside in silico study.
papers.abstract: A series of anti-inflammatory pyridine-benzofuran hybrid derivatives were synthesized from 2-acetylbenzofuran and natural aldehydes via a mild and efficient multicomponent reaction. Structures were confirmed using infrared (IR) and NMR spectroscopy. Anti-inflammatory effects were evaluated in the carrageenan-induced paw edema model in adult male rats. Among all tested compounds, 7a and 7e demonstrated the most potent dose-dependent inhibition, reaching 61.2% and 60.3% at 200 mg/kg (∗∗p < 0.001), respectively, compared with indomethacin (78.5% at 10 mg/kg). Molecular docking studies against the
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of pyridine-benzofuran hybrid compounds using a green multicomponent reaction and tested their anti-inflammatory activity in a rat paw edema model. Two compounds (7a and 7e) showed the strongest dose-dependent inhibition, reaching about 60% efficacy at 200 mg/kg, compared to indomethacin's 78.5% at 10 mg/kg. Molecular docking studies were also performed to explore potential binding interactions.

papers.title: Agmatine as the initiating substrate for aspartate semialdehyde-dependent bacterial spermidine biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: Putrescine has long been considered the initiating substrate for aspartate semialdehyde-dependent bacterial spermidine biosynthesis. However, two recent studies identified a variant pathway in which agmatine serves as the preferred substrate. This variation appears to be common, but the mechanistic basis for substrate preference was unknown. Here, we investigate the aspartate semialdehyde-dependent dehydrogenases from Bacteroides fragilis and Clostridium leptum using steady-state and transient-state kinetic assays, mass spectrometry, thermal shift protein stability assays, X-ray crystallograph
papers.summary: This study investigates the aspartate semialdehyde-dependent spermidine biosynthesis pathway in Bacteroides fragilis and Clostridium leptum, showing that agmatine rather than putrescine is the preferred initiating substrate. Using kinetics, mass spectrometry, stability assays, and X-ray crystallography, the authors reveal the mechanistic basis for this substrate preference, which appears to be a common variant in bacteria.

papers.title: Functional unknomics of the SAR11 clade reveal hidden genetic potential underlying adaptation to bottom-up and top-down pressures.
papers.abstract: A substantial fraction of the genes in bacteria lack detectable sequence similarity to genes with known functions. These functionally uncharacterized genes-collectively referred to as the "unknome"-represent a largely unexplored genetic repertoire harboring insights into marine bacterial ecology. In this study, we explored the function of the unknome of the SAR11 clade, the most abundant bacterial lineage in the ocean, with a particular focus on genes that provide insight into its ecology. Based on the Clusters of Orthologous Genes and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes classifications, a
papers.summary: This study systematically investigates the 'unknome'—genes with no known function—in the SAR11 clade, the most abundant marine bacterial lineage. By analyzing these uncharacterized genes, the authors uncover hidden genetic potential linked to how SAR11 adapts to bottom-up (resource availability) and top-down (predation, viral pressure) ecological pressures. The work highlights that a large portion of SAR11's genome remains functionally unexplored despite its ecological importance.

papers.title: Critical review of adsorption technologies for heavy metal removal: mechanistic, computational, and policy perspectives.
papers.abstract: The main sources of heavy metal pollution in groundwater include discharges from petroleum refining plants, agricultural runoff, hospital wastewater, and environmental damage caused by war. Advances in adsorbents provide safe, efficient, and economical techniques for contaminant removal. This study presents a critical review of adsorption applications worldwide, particularly in Iraq, evaluating the effectiveness, large-scale applicability, and long-term sustainability of selected adsorbents. Furthermore, the study focuses on adsorption mechanisms, criteria for selecting appropriate adsorbents,
papers.summary: This review critically examines adsorption technologies for removing heavy metals from groundwater, with a particular focus on applications in Iraq. It evaluates adsorbent effectiveness, scalability, and sustainability, while also covering adsorption mechanisms, adsorbent selection criteria, and policy considerations.

papers.title: Genolator enables protein function interpretation using a multimodal large language model fusing genomic and structural interpretation with natural language interaction.
papers.abstract: Decoding the genetic code to unveil its genome functionality is a monumental task which would greatly advance the understanding of disease mechanisms and development of targeted treatments. Although large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across diverse domains, translating the complex language of DNA into human-readable form remains challenging due to genomic data complexity and unexplored regions of the human genome. Current language models either are capable of processing natural language or the genomic code. Models fusing both aspects are largely lacking.
papers.summary: Genolator is a multimodal large language model that integrates genomic sequence data with protein structural information and natural language interaction to interpret protein function. It addresses the gap where existing models handle either natural language or genomic code but not both, aiming to translate DNA variants into human-readable functional insights relevant to disease mechanisms and targeted treatments.

papers.title: Active-site arginines differentially control Cas12a DNA cleavage and specificity.
papers.abstract: Cas12a is a CRISPR-Cas nuclease with biochemical features that make it useful for genome editing and nucleic acid diagnostics. However, its off-target and non-specific trans and CRISPR RNA-independent DNA cleavages can reduce the accuracy and limit applications requiring high fidelity. Here, we analyzed the role of two conserved arginine residues, R918 and R921, found in the RuvC active site pocket of Francisella novicida Cas12a. Through amino acid substitutions, biochemical assays, kinetic analysis, and computational study, we establish that a positive charge at 921 is required for CRISPR RNA
papers.summary: This study investigates two conserved arginine residues (R918 and R921) in the RuvC active site of Francisella novicida Cas12a, showing they play distinct roles in DNA cleavage and specificity. A positive charge at position 921 is required for CRISPR RNA-guided cleavage, while substitutions at these positions differentially affect off-target and non-specific cleavage activities. These findings reveal how active-site arginines can be tuned to improve Cas12a fidelity for genome editing and diagnostics.

papers.title: Structure-informed theoretical modeling defines principles governing avidity in bivalent protein interactions.
papers.abstract: In signaling cascades, signaling proteins often encode multiple domains or motifs, which presents the possibility for avidity -- where multivalent binding drastically increases interaction strength and duration. However, predicting and validating multivalent interactions that interact with avidity is a challenge. Here, we integrate mechanistic modeling, structure-based analysis, and experimental approaches as a framework for defining the conditions under which avidity plays a role. We explore the tandem SH2 domain family of interactions with bisphosphorylated partners as a multivalent archetyp
papers.summary: This paper develops a structure-informed theoretical framework combining mechanistic modeling, structural analysis, and experiments to predict when avidity—enhanced binding from multivalent interactions—governs bivalent protein interactions. Using tandem SH2 domains binding bisphosphorylated partners as a model system, the authors define the conditions under which avidity significantly strengthens and prolongs interactions. The work provides principles for predicting multivalent binding that could guide interpretation of signaling complexes and design of avidity-based binders.

papers.title: An integrative computational and experimental evaluation of natural compounds with potential to target LuxS in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
papers.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KPn) has emerged as a major global health concern due to increasing antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The development of new antimicrobial agents is essential to address multidrug-resistant and emerging hypervirulent strains associated with increased morbidity and mortality worldwide. In this study, an integrative computational-experimental approach was employed to characterise the anti-quorum sensing and anti-biofilm activities of selected natural compounds targeting the LuxS/autoinducer-2 (AI-2) system in KPn. Six compounds were initially screened using homology modellin
papers.summary: This study combines computational screening (homology modeling, docking) with experimental validation to identify natural compounds that inhibit the LuxS/AI-2 quorum-sensing system in Klebsiella pneumoniae. The goal is to find new anti-virulence agents that disrupt biofilm formation and could help combat multidrug-resistant strains.

papers.title: Hybrid density functional study of strain-engineered III-V semiconductors and monolayer InSe.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of strain-dependent semiconductor properties requires reliable exchange-correlation treatments and a unified understanding of bulk and two-dimensional materials. Here, we investigate strain-engineered bulk AlP, AlSb, and monolayer InSe under biaxial strains from -6% to +6% using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) and Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof (HSE06) functionals. HSE06 significantly improves structural accuracy, reducing the mean absolute deviation in lattice parameters from 1.47% to 0.39%. Biaxial strain lowers the symmetry of bulk AlP and AlSb from cubic zinc blende to tetrag
papers.summary: This study uses hybrid density functional theory (HSE06) to model how biaxial strain affects the electronic and structural properties of bulk AlP, AlSb, and monolayer InSe. HSE06 substantially improves lattice parameter accuracy over standard PBE, reducing mean absolute deviation from 1.47% to 0.39%, and reveals strain-induced symmetry lowering in the bulk III-V compounds.

papers.title: Probe-Atom Distributions Obtained from Mixed-Solvent Molecular Dynamics Improve the Scoring of Docking Calculations.
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used for the computational selection of drug candidates from compound libraries. Protein-ligand docking calculations are often performed as key steps in the early stages of this process. However, current docking calculations have limited accuracy. Thus, improvements are needed to more efficiently identify promising drug candidates. In this study, we performed mixed-solvent molecular dynamics (MSMD) simulations using four types of probe molecules to improve the accuracy of large-scale VS. We proposed a method for the modification of the docking s
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study uses mixed-solvent molecular dynamics (MSMD) simulations with four types of probe molecules to map where different chemical groups preferentially bind on a protein surface. These probe-atom distributions are then incorporated into docking scoring, improving the accuracy of structure-based virtual screening for drug candidate selection.

papers.title: PockLigGPT: Pocket-Sequence-Conditioned Molecular Generation with GPTs and RL.
papers.abstract: De novo drug design aims to generate molecules targeting specific protein pockets while retaining chemical plausibility and drug-like properties. Recent 3D structure-based generative methods explicitly model pocket-ligand geometry, but this does not always translate into chemically realistic or practically usable candidate molecules. Molecular language models provide a complementary sequence-based alternative. However, it remains unclear whether sequence-based pocket information can effectively guide ligand generation, whether multistage training improves pocket-specific generation, and whethe
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: PockLigGPT introduces a pocket-sequence-conditioned molecular generation framework that combines GPT-based language models with reinforcement learning to design drug-like molecules targeting specific protein pockets. The work investigates whether sequence-based pocket representations can effectively guide ligand generation and whether multistage training improves pocket-specific molecule quality, offering a complementary approach to 3D structure-based generative methods.

papers.title: Structural Overview of GLP-1 Analogs.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogs exert potent metabolic effects through structural features that govern receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. Key structural determinants include N-terminal modifications that confer resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 degradation, as well as C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize peptide helicity and enhance GLP-1 receptor affinity. Lipidation and albumin-binding strategies prolong systemic exposure by increasing circulating half-life, forming the basis of long-acting agents such as liraglutide and semaglutide. Structural variat
papers.summary: This review summarizes how the structural features of GLP-1 analogs—such as N-terminal modifications that resist DPP-4 degradation, C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize helicity, and lipidation strategies that extend half-life—determine their receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. These structural principles underlie the design of long-acting agents like liraglutide and semaglutide.

papers.title: Multiscale Explainable Machine Learning Reveals Descriptor-Invariant Molecular Determinants of Small-Molecule PD-1/PD-L1 Inhibition.
papers.abstract: The PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint pathway is a major target in cancer immunotherapy; however, small-molecule inhibitor development remains challenging due to the hydrophobic, structurally shallow PD-L1 interface. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based QSAR framework to identify determinants governing PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition. A data set of 844 compounds, represented using MACCS, PubChem, and Mordred descriptors, was modeled using multiple machine learning algorithms with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) models achieving the
papers.summary: The authors built an explainable machine learning QSAR framework using 844 small molecules to identify molecular features that determine PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition, testing multiple descriptor sets (MACCS, PubChem, Mordred) and algorithms. XGBoost and LightGBM performed best, and the explainability analysis revealed descriptor-invariant molecular determinants of inhibitory activity. This offers guidance for designing small-molecule immune checkpoint inhibitors despite the challenging shallow, hydrophobic PD-L1 interface.

papers.title: Covalent Stabilizers of the Interaction Between 14-3-3σ and Estrogen Receptor‑α.
papers.abstract: Selective stabilization of complexes formed by the hub protein 14-3-3 represents an emerging mechanism for the modulation of therapeutically relevant targets. In this letter, we describe a hit-finding campaign designed to identify small molecule stabilizers of the interaction between 14-3-3σ and the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα). Four structurally distinct hits were identified and validated using a combination of biochemical assays and biophysical techniques. Ternary complex crystal structures revealed that all four hit compounds form a covalent bond with Cys38 of 14-3-3σ via four different el
papers.summary: This study reports the discovery of small molecules that covalently stabilize the protein-protein interaction between 14-3-3σ and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα). Four structurally distinct hit compounds were identified and validated biochemically and biophysically, with crystal structures showing each forms a covalent bond with Cys38 of 14-3-3σ. This demonstrates a new strategy for modulating ERα activity through covalent stabilization of a hub-protein complex.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) by rationally modifying the deaminase and adding a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, aiming to boost its cytosine base editing efficiency while retaining its low off-target profile. This addresses the main limitation of the original tBE, which had reduced off-target mutations but modest editing efficiency.

papers.title: Pharmacological modulation of GPR84 revealed by dual states structures and immune functional assays.
papers.abstract: G-protein-coupled receptor 84 (GPR84) is an orphan class A GPCR selectively activated by medium chain fatty acids and highly expressed in immune cells, where it modulates pro-inflammatory signaling. The structural basis of GPR84 inactivation and antagonism has remained unclear, limiting the rational design of pathway-selective modulators despite its clinical relevance in metabolic inflammation and fibrotic diseases. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy structures of human GPR84 in inactive and active states. The 3.5 Å inactive structure bound to the antagonist GLPG1205 reveals a lid-like c
papers.summary: This study presents cryo-electron microscopy structures of the orphan GPCR GPR84 in both inactive (antagonist-bound) and active states, revealing the structural basis for its inactivation and antagonism. Combined with immune functional assays, the work identifies key conformational features that could guide rational design of pathway-selective modulators for inflammatory and fibrotic diseases.

papers.title: Biological Investigation of Novel Pyrazole-Based Anticancer Scaffolds: A Trinity of Synthetic Methodologies on Computational Assessment of IC50 Against Human Cancer Cell Lines MCF-7, MDA-MB and HeLa.
papers.abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is a key regulator of mitotic progression and is frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, making it an attractive therapeutic target for the development of targeted anticancer agents. The present study aimed to design and synthesize sixteen novel pyrazole derivatives (Pz-01 to Pz-16) as potential AURKA-targeted anticancer agents and to evaluate their anticancer activity, AURKA-binding potential, and SAR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. The synthesized compounds were screened for cytotoxic activity against human breast cancer (MCF-7 and
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized sixteen novel pyrazole derivatives as potential Aurora kinase A (AURKA) inhibitors for cancer therapy. The compounds were tested for cytotoxicity against breast cancer (MCF-7, MDA-MB) and cervical cancer (HeLa) cell lines, with computational docking and SAR analysis used to assess AURKA binding and guide structure optimization. The work identifies pyrazole scaffolds as promising leads for targeted anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Macrocyclization of Broad-Spectrum Kinase Inhibitor Bosutinib Leads to Potent and Selective Quinoline-Based HIPK4 Inhibitor AZ137.
papers.abstract: Homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 4 (HIPK4) remains an understudied member of the dark kinome. While genetic knockout studies suggest its involvement in spermiogenesis and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, whether these cellular functions can be recapitulated by pharmacological inhibition remains to be determined. These investigations are currently hampered by a lack of high-quality chemical tools. To address this, we employed a rational design strategy utilizing macrocyclization of a bosutinib-based scaffold. Systematic optimization led to the discovery of AZ137 (28e), a potent and sele
papers.summary: The authors used macrocyclization of the broad-spectrum kinase inhibitor bosutinib to develop AZ137, a potent and selective inhibitor of HIPK4, an understudied kinase in the 'dark kinome'. This compound provides a much-needed chemical tool to probe HIPK4's roles in spermiogenesis and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

papers.title: Enhancing biocatalytic retrosynthesis with a graph-to-graph model.
papers.abstract: Biocatalytic synthesis offers a green and sustainable route for chemical production, yet the rational design of biocatalytic routes remains challenging due to the need to jointly consider reaction feasibility and enzymatic compatibility. Here, we present BioG2G_ESR, a unified framework centered on graph-to-graph modeling for single-step biocatalytic retrosynthesis, with enzyme sequence recommendation as a downstream extension. BioG2G formulates retrosynthesis as a graph-to-graph translation task, directly predicting reactant molecular graphs from product structures while preserving molecular t
papers.summary: The authors present BioG2G_ESR, a graph-to-graph machine learning framework for single-step biocatalytic retrosynthesis that directly predicts reactant molecular graphs from product structures while also recommending compatible enzyme sequences. This unified approach jointly addresses reaction feasibility and enzymatic compatibility, which are typically handled separately in rational biocatalytic route design.

papers.title: Domain-Swapped LuxR-Type Quorum Sensing Receptors Reveal Divergent Ligand-Response Mechanisms among Homologues.
papers.abstract: LuxI/R quorum sensing controls diverse cell density-dependent behaviors in gram-negative bacteria, yet the molecular basis of LuxR-type receptor response to ligands remains poorly defined. This gap limits both mechanistic understanding of signaling and the rational design of synthetic LuxR modulators. LuxR homologues exhibit two response modes: associative receptors require N-acyl l-homoserine lactone (AHL) signal binding to enable DNA binding and transcriptional activation, whereas dissociative receptors are active without ligand and inhibited upon AHL binding. Herein, we dissect determinants
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This study uses domain-swapped LuxR-type quorum sensing receptors to dissect how homologous receptors achieve opposite ligand-response modes: associative receptors require AHL binding to activate transcription, while dissociative receptors are active without ligand and inhibited by AHL. The work reveals divergent molecular determinants underlying these two signaling behaviors, offering a framework for understanding and engineering LuxR-based signaling.

papers.title: Accessible hybrid DFT-quality NMR crystallography via gas-phase machine learning interatomic potentials.
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) crystallography is a robust method for structure determination, but its reliance on density functional theory (DFT) calculations for geometry refinement limits its speed and accessibility. Recent machine-learning predictors such as ShiftML3 can evaluate magnetic shieldings in seconds, but still need high-quality crystal geometries that are normally obtained from slow DFT optimisations. Here, we demonstrate that machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can eliminate this bottleneck for organic crystals. Interestingly, models trained on gas-phase molecules
papers.summary: This paper shows that machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained on gas-phase molecules can replace slow DFT geometry optimizations in NMR crystallography for organic crystals. This makes hybrid DFT-quality NMR crystallography much faster and more accessible, since MLIPs provide the high-quality crystal geometries needed by fast ML shielding predictors like ShiftML3.

papers.title: Rational Design of Au@co-MOF Synergistic Platform for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Dopamine in Human Biological Fluids.
papers.abstract: This study presents the rational design and application of engineered metal-organic framework (MOF) hybrids, tailored to exhibit accelerated electron transfer kinetics and enhanced molecular recognition capabilities for the high-sensitivity detection of dopamine (DA). Specifically, an enzyme-free electrochemical sensing platform was constructed using Au@Co-MOF nanocomposites, which were synthesized via a controllable in situ growth approach. Au nanoparticles (AuNPs) were uniformly anchored onto the [Co3(TMA)3(H2O)5]n (where TMA = 1,3,5-trimesic acid) framework containing coordinatively unsatur
papers.summary: This study reports an enzyme-free electrochemical sensor built from gold nanoparticle-decorated cobalt metal-organic framework (Au@Co-MOF) nanocomposites for detecting dopamine in human biological fluids. The engineered hybrid shows accelerated electron transfer and improved molecular recognition, enabling ultrasensitive dopamine quantification. The work demonstrates a rational design strategy for MOF-based sensing platforms in clinical diagnostics.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Novel Leads as Potential DPP-IV Inhibitors as Antidiabetic Agents Using Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) is a validated therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes mellitus due to its role in incretin hormone degradation. This study aimed to identify novel small-molecule DPP-IV inhibitors from the ECBD database using an integrated virtual screening and molecular dynamics (MD) approach, acknowledging that experimental validation is necessary to confirm biological activity. Methods: Structure-based virtual screening of 5,500 ECBD compounds was performed using molecular docking to identify high-affinity ligands, followed by interaction analysis with key catalytic
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 5,500 compounds from the ECBD database against DPP-IV, a validated target for type 2 diabetes. Several high-affinity candidate inhibitors were identified through interaction analysis with key catalytic residues, though the authors note that experimental validation is still required to confirm biological activity.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) on three Alzheimer's disease targets under both redocking and cross-docking conditions. The results show that success determinants differ between the two classes of methods, with AI approaches performing well in redocking but physics-based methods showing distinct advantages under realistic cross-docking scenarios.

papers.title: Drug Design Studio (DDS) 2.0: A Unified Platform for Network Pharmacology Integrated with Docking and Virtual Screening Workflow for Covalent/Non-Covalent Binders.
papers.abstract: Network pharmacology has become a central paradigm in modern drug discovery, replacing the reductionist "one drug, one target" view with a systems-level understanding of how compounds engage networks of proteins that are linked to disease. Despite its impact, a typical network-pharmacology study remains fragmented and technically demanding: researchers must query several independent databases, install and reconcile multiple standalone tools for target collection, network construction, hub-gene ranking and pathway enrichment, and then manually bridge the results into structure-based follow-up s
papers.summary: DDS 2.0 is a unified software platform that integrates network pharmacology with molecular docking and virtual screening, allowing researchers to go from compound-target network analysis to structure-based evaluation of covalent and non-covalent binders in one workflow. It addresses the fragmentation of typical network pharmacology studies, where multiple databases and standalone tools must be manually reconciled.

papers.title: A resource-efficient structure-based workflow for fragment progression enables parallel hit discovery and validation of functionally diverse modulators of NCS-1 protein-protein interactions.
papers.abstract: Efficient drug discovery workflows ideally generate data that directly address key translational milestones, including confirmation of target engagement and binding pose, structure-activity relationships (SARs), and biological relevance, within rapid and resource-efficient experimental cycles. Here, we describe a data-driven, automation-assisted, customizable framework for fragment-to-hit progression that directly delivers structurally validated hit series primed for rapid SAR exploration by exploiting the high-throughput crystallography available at synchrotrons. This recently evolved direct-
papers.summary: The authors present a resource-efficient, structure-based workflow for progressing fragments to hits, leveraging high-throughput synchrotron crystallography and automation to rapidly validate binding poses and generate SAR data. They apply it to discover functionally diverse modulators of NCS-1 protein-protein interactions, demonstrating parallel hit discovery and validation.

papers.title: Substrate Recognition Analysis in an Ethyl Carbamate-Hydrolyzing Esterase and Semi-Rational Baijiu Flavor Preservation.
papers.abstract: Ethyl carbamate (EC) is a widely recognized carcinogen present in fermented foods, and enzymatic degradation is a safe and effective strategy for its reduction. An EC-degrading esterase derived from Acinetobacter calcoaceticus (AcECH) was previously identified. However, volatile ester compounds in Chinese Baijiu compete with EC for enzyme binding, thereby affecting degradation efficiency and flavor quality. In this study, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enzyme kinetics, bio-layer interferometry (BLI), and gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) were employ
papers.summary: This study investigates how an ethyl carbamate-degrading esterase (AcECH) from Acinetobacter calcoaceticus interacts with competing volatile ester compounds found in Chinese Baijiu. Using molecular docking, MD simulations, enzyme kinetics, BLI, and GC-IMS, the authors characterize substrate recognition and propose a semi-rational strategy to preserve Baijiu flavor while reducing the carcinogen ethyl carbamate.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys over 80 computational tools for bacteriophage research, most published since 2020, covering tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive computational paradigms—sequence homology, machine learning, and emerging approaches—and discusses the limitations of each, such as database completeness and availability of labelled training data. The review is aimed at experienced practitioners and developers seeking a structured overview of phage bioinformatics.

papers.title: HighFold4: extending AlphaFold3 to accurate cyclic peptide conformation prediction via custom chemical connectivity.
papers.abstract: While AlphaFold3 has revolutionized protein structure prediction and supports noncanonical amino acids, its architecture always fails to reliably generate the closed-ring topologies characteristic of cyclic peptides. Existing adaptations, such as imposing distance constraints via an offset matrix, enforce ring geometry but cannot specify the chemical identity of the cyclization bond, leading to a restrictive bias toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles. Here, we present HighFold4, a framework that adapts AlphaFold3 to explicitly incorporate user-defined chemical connectivity between resi
papers.summary: HighFold4 extends AlphaFold3 to accurately predict cyclic peptide conformations by allowing users to explicitly specify the chemical connectivity of the cyclization bond, rather than relying on generic distance constraints. This overcomes AlphaFold3's bias toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles and enables modeling of diverse ring topologies. The framework broadens AlphaFold3's applicability to noncanonical cyclic peptides relevant to drug discovery.

papers.title: Structure-based virulence factor classification using a dual-driven graph transformer with a pretrained language model.
papers.abstract: Bacterial pathogenicity relies on a multitude of virulence factors (VFs). Identifying these factors is crucial for comprehending the molecular mechanisms driving bacterial pathogenesis and pinpointing potential targets for antivirulence strategies. While the identification of VFs has received extensive attention, there is still a lack of prediction from the perspective of VF classes. Moreover, most computational methods focus solely on sequence information for virulence proteins, neglecting spatial structure information. Here, a novel Structure-based Dual-driven Graph Transformer framework nam
papers.summary: The paper introduces a structure-based dual-driven graph transformer framework that incorporates a pretrained protein language model to classify bacterial virulence factors into specific functional classes. By integrating both sequence and spatial structural information, the method improves prediction of virulence factor categories compared to sequence-only approaches. This could aid in understanding bacterial pathogenesis and identifying targets for antivirulence therapies.

papers.title: Integrative In Silico Profiling of Major Phytochemicals From a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum Mixture: Docking, Molecular Dynamics, ADMET, and Ligand-Based Target Prediction on Shared Pathways in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) converge through metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and impaired neuronal signaling, providing a rationale for multi-target intervention. This study aimed to identify phytochemicals from a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum mixture that may modulate this disease axis. Seven constituents were screened against AChE, BACE1, DPP4, glucokinase, GSK3β, and TACE using molecular docking and MM-GBSA rescoring. Prioritized complexes underwent triplicate 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, post-MD MM-GBSA analysis, physicoch
papers.summary: This study used computational docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET profiling to screen seven phytochemicals from a three-plant mixture against six protein targets shared between type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease. The work identifies candidate compounds that may modulate both metabolic and neurodegenerative pathways, though experimental validation is lacking.

papers.title: Computational, In Vitro, and In Vivo Evaluation of Benzimidazole-Pyrazole Hybrid Scaffolds as Multi-Target Anti-Ulcer Agents.
papers.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) continues to be an important gastrointestinal condition attributed to Helicobacter pylori infection, usage of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, oxidative stress, and inflammatory mediators. Although there are available treatments for this condition, side effects, relapse, and safety issues call for development of new multi-target anti-ulcer compounds. In this research, a group of benzimidazole-pyrazole analogs (5a-5j) was designed, synthesized, and studied with the aid of computational and experimental methods. Molecular docking into H+/K+-ATPase (PDB ID: 5YLU) a
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of benzimidazole-pyrazole hybrid compounds (5a-5j) and evaluated them as multi-target anti-ulcer agents using molecular docking against H+/K+-ATPase, in vitro assays, and in vivo models. The work aims to address limitations of current peptic ulcer treatments, such as side effects and relapse, by targeting multiple pathways involved in ulcer pathology.

papers.title: Investigation of In Vitro α-Amylase Inhibitory, Antioxidant, Phytochemical Profiling, Molecular Docking, and Swiss ADME Analysis of Magnolia zotictla.
papers.abstract: The current study was carried out to determine the in vitro antioxidant and antidiabetic potential and phytochemical profiling of crude extract obtained from the cone of Magnolia zotictla, and then to integrate it with computational chemistry. Phytochemical profiling was determined via HPLC and GC-MS analysis. In HPLC analysis, five compounds were identified, while five compounds were identified through GC-MS. The plant extract exhibited good antioxidant efficacy in the DPPH assay, highlighting its capacity to neutralize free radicals. The extract has an IC50 value of 123.8 µg/mL, while that o
papers.summary: This study characterizes the phytochemical composition of Magnolia zotictla cone extract using HPLC and GC-MS, identifying ten compounds, and evaluates its antioxidant and α-amylase inhibitory activities in vitro. Molecular docking and Swiss ADME analyses were used to predict binding interactions and drug-likeness of the identified compounds, suggesting potential antidiabetic and antioxidant applications.

papers.title: Synergistic Zundel-Eigen mechanism for proton transport in protic ionic liquids unraveled by machine learning force fields and NMR spectra.
papers.abstract: Elucidating proton transfer in nonaqueous media is essential for the rational design of advanced chemical processes and energy materials, yet its molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. Here, we combine machine-learning potential-based molecular dynamics, path-integral molecular dynamics simulations and metadynamics, and ¹H NMR spectroscopy to investigate proton-transfer dynamics in choline-amino acid protic ionic liquids. We show that proton migration occurs across a continuum of transient solvation motifs, including Eigen-like, Zundel-like, and intermediate configurations, with interm
papers.summary: This study uses machine-learning force fields and NMR spectroscopy to reveal that proton transport in choline-amino acid protic ionic liquids proceeds through a synergistic Zundel-Eigen mechanism involving a continuum of transient solvation states. The findings provide a detailed molecular picture of proton transfer in nonaqueous media, which is important for designing advanced energy materials and chemical processes.

papers.title: Engineering the Stability of Sucrose Synthase to Enable Efficient Coupled Production of UDP-Glucuronic Acid.
papers.abstract: The biocatalytic synthesis of UDP-glucuronic acid (UDPGA), a key precursor for glucuronides and high-value carbohydrates, is limited by an unstable UDP-glucose (UDPG) supply in coupled systems. In this study, through an extensive screening of 10 sucrose synthases derived from both eukaryotic and prokaryotic microorganisms, we identified a broad-spectrum, highly efficient enzymatic scaffold suitable for the synthesis of UDP-sugars. A rational design integrating PROSS and ThermoMPNN algorithms with molecular dynamics (MD) analysis yielded the V353L mutant, which retained 97% of wild-type activit
papers.summary: This study screened 10 sucrose synthases to find a stable, efficient enzyme for producing UDP-glucuronic acid, a valuable precursor for glucuronides and carbohydrates. Using computational design (PROSS, ThermoMPNN, and molecular dynamics), they engineered a V353L mutant that retained 97% of wild-type activity while improving stability, enabling more efficient coupled production of UDPGA.

papers.title: Preparation, Structural Features, Bioactivities, and Food Application of Oyster Mushroom Polysaccharides: A Review.
papers.abstract: Water-soluble oyster mushroom polysaccharides (OMPs) are multifunctional biopolymers with growing relevance in food and health-related applications. This review summarizes recent progress in the extraction, purification, structural features, biological activities, and food applications of OMPs, with particular emphasis on tentative structure-activity relationships constrained by heterogeneous experimental evidence. Conventional and emerging extraction approaches, including hot water, enzyme-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, and microwave-assisted methods, are compared in terms of yield and struct
papers.summary: This review consolidates recent research on water-soluble polysaccharides from oyster mushrooms, covering extraction and purification methods, structural characterization, biological activities, and food applications. It highlights tentative structure-activity relationships while noting that heterogeneous experimental evidence limits firm conclusions. The paper serves as a reference for researchers and food scientists interested in these multifunctional biopolymers.

papers.title: Chitosan activates a sequential Ca 2+ -ROS-NO-jasmonate signaling cascade governing withanolide accumulation in Withania somnifera.
papers.abstract: Chitosan promotes withanolide accumulation in W. somnifera; however, the temporal organization of the underlying signaling network remains unresolved. We examined whether calcium (Ca2⁺), reactive oxygen species (ROS), nitric oxide (NO), and jasmone form an ordered cascade linking elicitor perception to specialized metabolism. Sixty-day-old greenhouse-grown plants were treated with 100 mg L-1 foliar chitosan alone or after pretreatment with LaCl₃, diphenyleneiodonium, cPTIO, or diethyldithiocarbamate, with inhibitor-only controls. Cytosolic Ca2+ -dependent fluorescence, NADPH oxidase activity,
papers.summary: This study shows that chitosan treatment in Withania somnifera triggers a sequential signaling cascade—calcium influx, then reactive oxygen species, then nitric oxide, then jasmonate—that ultimately boosts production of withanolides, the plant's medicinally important specialized metabolites. Using pharmacological inhibitors, the authors establish the ordering of these signaling events, clarifying how an external elicitor is translated into increased secondary metabolite biosynthesis.

papers.title: The substrate envelope strategy: Structural basis for resistance mitigation in antiviral drug design.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance remains a major hurdle in antiviral drug development. This review highlights the "substrate envelope hypothesis", a structure-based drug design (SBDD) paradigm that constrains the spatial boundaries and binding footprint of inhibitors within the conserved active site volume defined by natural viral substrates. By restricting inhibitor interactions to evolutionarily conserved residues, this approach ensures that mutations abrogating drug binding simultaneously impair natural substrate processing. This imposes an insurmountable fitness cost on the virus, thereby mitigating resist
papers.summary: This review describes the substrate envelope hypothesis, a structure-based drug design strategy that confines antiviral inhibitors to the conserved active-site volume occupied by natural viral substrates. Because resistance mutations that disrupt drug binding would also impair natural substrate processing, the approach imposes a fitness cost on the virus and helps mitigate resistance. The paper synthesizes structural evidence supporting this paradigm for antiviral development.

papers.title: HDX-MS-Guided computational modeling for rapid and accurate antibody-antigen interface mapping.
papers.abstract: Accurate mapping of paratopes and epitopes at antibody-antigen (Ab-Ag) interfaces is essential for the rational design of therapeutic antibodies in early drug development. Traditional methods for determining high-resolution Ab-Ag complex structures, such as X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy, are labor-intensive and require substantial time and resources. Although recent computational approaches have increased throughput, prediction accuracy and reliability remain limited, particularly without experimental structural constraints. Here, we present a hydrogen-deuterium exchange m
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational workflow that uses hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data as experimental constraints to guide antibody-antigen interface modeling, aiming to map paratopes and epitopes more rapidly and accurately than structure-determination methods like X-ray crystallography or cryo-EM. The approach addresses the limited reliability of purely computational interface prediction by anchoring predictions in experimental structural data.

papers.title: Mechanistic inhibition of herpes simplex virus-1 UL21 immune-evasion function by natural-product scaffolds: A multi-tier docking, dynamics, and energetic profiling approach.
papers.abstract: Alpha-herpesviruses, particularly herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), establish lifelong latency and employ multiple strategies to evade host immunity, thereby sustaining infection. A key mediator of this immune evasion is the viral tegument protein, unique long 21 (UL21), which disrupts the host cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) signaling pathway and suppresses antiviral type-I interferon responses, facilitating viral replication. Despite its important role in HSV-1 pathogenesis, UL21 remains an underexplored therapeutic target. This study aimed to identify
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding energy calculations to screen natural-product compounds for their ability to inhibit the HSV-1 tegument protein UL21, which normally suppresses host antiviral immunity via the cGAS-STING pathway. The authors identify natural-product scaffolds that bind UL21 and could potentially restore interferon responses against the virus. The work is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Therapeutic Potential of Natural Peptides Against Hemagglutinin-Esterase of Bovine Coronavirus Based on Molecular Dynamics Simulation Studies.
papers.abstract: The hemagglutinin-esterase (HE) protein of bovine coronavirus is required for virus attachment and entry into host cells. It is thus an attractive target for the development of peptide-based antiviral agents. In the present study, molecular docking was performed to identify bioactive peptides with high binding potential toward the HE protein, followed by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. A total of 16 bioactive peptides were initially evaluated by molecular docking, and 3 peptides with favorable interactions at the HE protein functional site were subsequently subjected to MD simulations. Af
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 16 natural bioactive peptides for their ability to bind the hemagglutinin-esterase (HE) protein of bovine coronavirus, a key protein for viral attachment and entry. Three peptides showed favorable interactions at the HE functional site and were further analyzed by MD simulations, suggesting they may have potential as peptide-based antiviral agents. The work is computational and preliminary, with no experimental validation reported.

papers.title: In silico analysis of MALAT1 and H19 lncRNA interactions with the diabetes-related proteins ASK1 and YAP1.
papers.abstract: Dysregulation of RNA-protein signalling networks contributes to the progression of diabetes-associated complications, yet the structural mechanisms underlying lncRNA interactions with key signalling proteins remain largely unknown. This study investigates potential interaction interfaces between MALAT1-ASK1 and H19-YAP1 using a hypothesis-generating in silico approach. A computational pipeline integrating structure prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations was employed. Structural assessment showed high local confidence for both proteins and lncRNAs (PAE < 1 Å) but low
papers.summary: This study uses computational structure prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to model potential interaction interfaces between the long non-coding RNAs MALAT1 and H19 and the diabetes-related proteins ASK1 and YAP1. The authors report high local structural confidence for the predicted molecules but note limitations in overall confidence, framing the work as hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive. The findings suggest possible lncRNA-protein interfaces that could inform future experimental studies on diabetes-associated signaling.

papers.title: DDA: a traceable multi-agent framework for automated structure-based drug design.
papers.abstract: Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD) is a key computational paradigm that uses protein structural information to design and optimize small molecules with desired binding properties. Existing SBDD methods mainly focus on molecular design and often lack the capability to independently conduct downstream evaluation and optimize workflows. Meanwhile, directly applying large language models (LLMs) to molecular design faces challenges such as fragmented execution, limited tool coordination, and insufficient traceability of intermediate decision-making processes. To address these limitations, we propos
papers.summary: The paper introduces DDA, a traceable multi-agent framework that automates structure-based drug design by coordinating specialized agents and tools around protein structures. It aims to overcome the fragmented execution and poor traceability of directly applying LLMs to molecular design by making intermediate decisions auditable. The framework integrates molecular design with downstream evaluation and workflow optimization.

papers.title: Integrated follicular fluid multi-omics identifies steroidogenic dysregulation and a candidate SHBG-associated rescue framework in poor ovarian response.
papers.abstract: Poor ovarian response (POR) remains a major obstacle in assisted reproductive technology, yet the follicular microenvironmental determinants of impaired ovarian sensitivity are poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize the multi_omics landscape of the follicular fluid in POR and to explore potential therapeutic candidates and underlying mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data from follicular fluid to characterize the microenvironment in poor ovarian response (POR), a common cause of assisted reproduction failure. The authors identify steroidogenic dysregulation and propose a candidate SHBG-associated rescue framework, suggesting potential therapeutic targets for improving ovarian sensitivity.

papers.title: Computational prediction of a multi-epitope Human Metapneumovirus vaccine candidate through integrated reverse vaccinology and pan-genomic approaches.
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a primary cause of global respiratory infections yet no approved vaccine currently exists. This study computationally predicts a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using a diverse dataset of 65 HMPV sequences spanning five continents. Following the screening of lead proteins for antigenicity and virulence, fifteen highly conserved MHC-I, MHC-II and B-cell epitopes were prioritized. These were integrated with a putative L7/L12 adjuvant using optimized AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers to design three constructs (HMPV_V1-V3). Structural validation identified HMPV-V2 as the
papers.summary: This study computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidates against Human Metapneumovirus by screening 65 viral sequences from five continents for conserved antigenic epitopes. Fifteen MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes were linked with an L7/L12 adjuvant to create three constructs, with structural validation identifying HMPV-V2 as the most promising candidate. The work provides a preliminary in silico vaccine design that requires experimental validation.

papers.title: Associations between serum lactate and renal dysfunction in diabetic kidney disease: An exploratory analysis integrating animal experiments, clinical cohorts, and bioinformatic approaches.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major cause of end-stage renal disease, but the metabolic changes associated with its progression are still not well understood. Lactate, traditionally regarded as a byproduct of glycolysis, has been increasingly recognized in recent studies in association with broader metabolic and regulatory processes. This study aimed to evaluate the association between serum lactate and renal dysfunction in DKD and to explore candidate molecular pathways linking lactate-associated metabolic alterations to DKD-related renal injury using animal experiments, clinical cohort
papers.summary: This exploratory study integrates animal experiments, clinical cohort data, and bioinformatic analyses to examine whether serum lactate levels are associated with renal dysfunction in diabetic kidney disease. The authors identify candidate molecular pathways that may link lactate-related metabolic alterations to DKD-related kidney injury, suggesting lactate could serve as a biomarker or mechanistic contributor.

papers.title: Identification of differentially expressed lncRNAs and candidate ceRNA networks across Mastitis stages in Sahiwal cattle.
papers.abstract: Along with being a significant disease in dairy cattle which incurs economic loss, mastitis also affects a wide range of parameters that involve milk yield and quality. However, the role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the regulation of mastitis in distinct stages of the disease in Sahiwal cows is yet to be understood. This study characterised lncRNA expression profiles and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks across healthy, subclinical, and clinical mastitis stages using RNA-Seq data from milk somatic cells. Five biologically relevant ceRNA modules were identified: Five ceRNA modul
papers.summary: This study used RNA-Seq of milk somatic cells from Sahiwal cattle to profile long non-coding RNA expression across healthy, subclinical, and clinical mastitis stages. The authors identified five biologically relevant ceRNA (competing endogenous RNA) modules, revealing stage-specific lncRNA-mRNA regulatory networks that may underlie mastitis progression. These findings provide candidate lncRNAs and regulatory interactions for further study of mastitis mechanisms in dairy cattle.

papers.title: Leveraging bioinformatics approaches for drug repositioning in space radiation protection.
papers.abstract: The health effects of space radiation, primarily Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs), on humans remain largely unknown, with potential cardiovascular consequences posing a significant threat to astronauts on long-duration spaceflight missions. Currently, there are no established pharmacological countermeasures for GCR exposure. Drug repositioning offers a promising strategy to accelerate pharmaceutical research in space medicine. This study leverages existing bioinformatics techniques to identify and prioritize potential drug candidates associated with proteomic perturbations following simulated GCR e
papers.summary: This study applies bioinformatics methods to identify existing drugs that could be repurposed to protect astronauts from the cardiovascular effects of galactic cosmic ray (GCR) exposure during long-duration spaceflight. By analyzing proteomic changes induced by simulated GCR, the authors prioritize candidate compounds as potential pharmacological countermeasures, addressing a gap where no approved drugs currently exist for space radiation protection.

papers.title: Novel 1,4-Diazepane derivatives as amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregation inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the aggregation of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptides, particularly Aβ42 and Aβ40, which contribute to neurotoxicity and disease progression. The development of novel small molecule inhibitors capable of preventing Aβ aggregation represents a promising therapeutic strategy. We report the design, synthesis and evaluation of a novel class of 1,4-diazepanes as anti-amyloid agents.
papers.summary: This paper reports the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a new class of 1,4-diazepane small molecules as inhibitors of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptide aggregation, a key pathological process in Alzheimer's disease. The compounds target the aggregation of Aβ42 and Aβ40 peptides, which are linked to neurotoxicity and disease progression, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for AD.

papers.title: Impact of cigarette toxicants on sarcopenic obesity: An in silico network toxicology and molecular dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenic obesity (SO) is a geriatric metabolic syndrome characterized by muscle mass loss, muscle strength decline, and excessive fat accumulation. Nicotine and coal tar disrupt skeletal muscle homeostasis and lipid metabolism. This study aims to elucidate the relevant molecular mechanisms by which nicotine and coal tar trigger sarcopenic obesity using an integrated in silico approach.
papers.summary: This study uses in silico network toxicology and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how cigarette toxicants (nicotine and coal tar) may contribute to sarcopenic obesity, a condition combining muscle loss with excess fat accumulation. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways linking these toxicants to disrupted skeletal muscle homeostasis and lipid metabolism.

papers.title: Potential hazard assessment of 6PPD-quinone in the context of ulcerative colitis: network toxicology, machine learning, transcriptomic analysis, and preliminary In vivo validation.
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) poses potential systemic health risks, yet its toxicological impact on the intestinal tract, particularly in the context of ulcerative colitis (UC), remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate whether 6PPD-Q aggravates DSS-induced colitis and to identify candidate molecular events using integrative computational and experimental approaches.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone worsens ulcerative colitis, using network toxicology, machine learning, and transcriptomic analysis combined with preliminary in vivo validation in a DSS-induced colitis model. The authors identify candidate molecular events linking 6PPD-Q exposure to colitis aggravation, suggesting a potential environmental risk factor for inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Dual targeting of CD244 and CD2 by a viral-immunoevasin-guided engineered CD48-Fc mutant for T- and NK-cell modulation.
papers.abstract: Viruses encode immunoevasins that subvert host co-signaling pathways. CD244:CD48 and CD2:CD58 interactions are critical for NK- and T-cell effector responses. We previously identified a herpesvirus-encoded soluble CD48 homolog that functions as a decoy ligand for CD244 and dampens NK-cell activation. Here, we show that this viral protein, A43, also recognizes CD2, and we used its structural features to engineer human CD48-Fc variants with dual CD244/CD2 specificity. The optimized mutein, C5-Fc, which incorporates twelve A43-guided substitutions predicted by structure-based modeling to enhance
papers.summary: Researchers engineered a human CD48-Fc fusion protein (C5-Fc) with dual specificity for CD244 and CD2 by borrowing structural features from a herpesvirus immunoevasin called A43. This engineered mutein can simultaneously modulate both NK- and T-cell co-signaling pathways, potentially offering a new tool for immune regulation.

papers.title: Molecular states and interfacial interactions at solid-liquid interfaces: advances and challenges in multimodal characterization.
papers.abstract: Solid-liquid interfaces govern key functions in biosensing, catalysis, energy conversion, drug delivery, and organic electronic devices because molecular adsorption, hydration, charge regulation, and structural reorganization occur within an ultrathin interfacial region. However, these phenomena are intrinsically multiscale and multidimensional, involving strongly coupled variables such as mass, interfacial potential, molecular orientation, viscoelasticity, and local nanoscale heterogeneity. As a result, no single measurement technique can fully describe interfacial states or their dynamics. T
papers.summary: This review discusses how solid-liquid interfaces control processes in biosensing, catalysis, energy conversion, drug delivery, and organic electronics through molecular adsorption, hydration, and charge regulation within an ultrathin region. It argues that because interfacial phenomena are multiscale and involve coupled variables like mass, potential, molecular orientation, and viscoelasticity, no single measurement technique can fully characterize them, motivating multimodal characterization approaches.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict cancer-causing mutations specifically in DNA-binding proteins. It addresses the challenge of identifying driver mutations that disrupt protein-DNA interactions, which are difficult to detect experimentally. The tool aims to help prioritize potentially oncogenic mutations in this important protein class.

papers.title: Multi-state Structure Prediction of G Protein-Coupled Receptor Proteins via Prompting on AlphaFold.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), an essential family of transmembrane proteins, widely participate in signal transduction in organisms and have long been recognized as a major class of therapeutic targets. In structure-based drug design, high-resolution structures of GPCRs in both active and inactive states are essential for designing agonists and antagonists, respectively. However, obtaining experimental GPCR structures is costly, while homology modeling and artificial-intelligence-driven approaches including AlphaFold 2 and AlphaFold 3 often show reduced accuracy for active-state conform
papers.summary: This paper presents a method that uses prompt-based adaptation of AlphaFold to predict multiple conformational states (active and inactive) of GPCR proteins, addressing the tendency of standard AlphaFold to produce inaccurate active-state structures. The approach aims to support structure-based drug design by providing reliable state-specific GPCR models without costly experimental determination.

papers.title: A voyage of reprogrammable metabolic bioengineering reshapes plant defense: from editing tools to synthetic systems.
papers.abstract: Metabolic bioengineering has emerged as a transformative approach for reshaping plant defense by targeting intrinsic biosynthetic pathways to enhance immunity in modern agriculture. Moving beyond proof-of-concept metabolomics to broad-spectrum programmable pathway engineering addresses gaps in plant rational design and optimizes resilience in response to diverse environmental cues. This review aims to comprehensively highlight the transition of innovative approaches to phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids, inferring adaptive reprogramming that mediates the growth-de
papers.summary: This review surveys how metabolic bioengineering can be used to reprogram plant biosynthetic pathways—such as those producing phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids—to strengthen plant immunity. It traces the field's shift from proof-of-concept metabolomics toward programmable, broad-spectrum pathway engineering for more resilient crops.

papers.title: PLK1/FOXM1-associated tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) and forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) have been widely studied in various cancers; however, their expression characteristics in endometrial cancer (EC) and their potential association with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the expression patterns of PLK1 and FOXM1 in endometrial cancer and links them to a specific tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in the tumor microenvironment. The findings suggest these markers may help define tumor heterogeneity and immune interactions in endometrial cancer.
